sentences.text: Being aggrieved of the order dated 25.04.2019 passed in Cr.R. No.284/2018 by the Second Additional Judge, Bhopal to the Court of First Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal, whereby the learned Additional Sessions Judge has dismissed the criminal revision filed by the applicant and affirmed the order dated 11.06.2018 passed by the JMFC, Bhopal.

entities.text: Court of First Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The trial Court dismissed the private complaint filed by the applicant on the ground that there is no material available on the record to take cognizance against the respondents for the offence punishable under Section 406, 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of IPC.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that both the Courts below have failed to look that the accused has issued the cheque to the respondents for payment of Rs.10 Lacs which was dishonored because of insufficient funds which comes under the purview of Section 420 of the IPC because the accused were well aware of the fact that amount mentioned in the cheque, is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:2023 2 MCRC-28637-2019 insufficient in their account.
It is further submitted that both the Courts below have committed gross error in not taking cognizance against the respondents, though there was sufficient evidence available on record.

It is further submitted that petitioners are innocent villagers and they have been cheated by the respondents by conspiracy and therefore, trial Court ought to have took cognizance against the respondents.
4. I have carefully perused the orders passed by both the courts below and find that both the courts have passed reasoned orders.

I have also examined the complaint and the evidence produced before the Trial Court and find that no error, illegality, or perversity has been committed by the Trial Court in rejecting the complaint of the petitioner.

The wording of the agreement clearly indicates that,
upon performance of the agreement, the petitioner would have the right to pursue appropriate legal remedies and recover the amount by instituting a civil suit.
